source_record.bounded_interface_domain: The receiving criterion, observed failure or valid scope condition specifies a consequence or constraint on that asset policy. The named object, configuration, relevant time/population and actual receiving use are identified. Similar language, possible encoding, organizational co-use or an arbitrary tool does not establish a bridge. Unknown applicability remains unknown. A supported partial premise can be material while the whole receiving predicate remains unestablished.
source_record.domain_horizon_authority: The exact member object, configuration, observation interval, consequence and actual authority in each literal argument; no adoption or legal applicability inference.
source_record.evidence_ceiling: Sparse observations do not supply population failure estimates; maintenance does not establish arbitrary availability or safe recovery. Missing recovery does not erase a separately demonstrated reduction in exposed independent instances. Analytical native-role inference only; no empirical effect size, universal benefit, new historical descent or final scientific acceptance.
source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Maintenance labour and windows, downtime, spare stock, responders, configuration history, bad predictions, correlated failures, over-maintenance and single-expert dependency count. For a cheap noncritical item, run-to-failure with spares and tested replacement can be adequate.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: Generic co-use or arbitrary supporting tool rejected.
Whole receiving predicate failure does not erase a materially used partial input.
Every listed adverse control defeats the corresponding stronger whole-result inference.

positive_controls.argument: An interpretable verification method supplies evidence about the specific failure-detection or restoration claim on which the maintenance policy relies.
Integration and system observations can expose common causes or restoration order that changes the warranted maintenance/recovery policy.
Representative use identifies the consequential outage and recovery outcomes, constraining which maintenance policy is adequate for that use.
Qualified conditions, margins and configuration constraints delimit permissible maintenance substitutions and evidence reuse.
Actual delivery criteria and allowed residuals specify which repair/support evidence the policy must provide for this item.
The actual basis constrains accepted maintenance actions, configuration changes, inspection means and authorization roles.
Competent challenge can reveal an unjustified failure model, common cause, over-maintenance burden or untested recovery assumption and narrow the policy claim.
Current meaningful trace links identify which assets and assurance claims a repair, substitution or newly discovered defect actually affects.
Hazard timing, common causes and safe-state constraints identify which maintenance and restoration actions are permissible and consequential.
Claim structure identifies the exact failure or recovery proposition and conditions the maintenance policy must warrant.
Incident and recurrence evidence can reveal a failed maintenance assumption or repair that does not address the failure mechanism, prompting proportionate policy reassessment.
Representative rehearsal and deployment conditions expose whether the maintenance policy can operate within the real recovery and staffing constraints.
Versioned operational evidence and regression signals identify changed conditions requiring policy reassessment or updated restoration evidence.
Actual residual criteria, controlled resources and permitted actions delimit viable maintenance or recovery choices and expose who can authorize a deferral.
